newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan seen buying 54,000T soy/corn, 69,000T wheat.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan seen buying 54,000T soy/corn, 69,000T wheat.

text.p: High international prices mean Taiwanese buyers are likely to be lukewarm participants in grain and oilseed markets this week, traders said on Monday.
One tender for 54,000 tonnes of soybeans and corn and two shipments totalling 69,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat for the Taiwan Flour Mills Association are scheduled in the next few days.

A swift rally in Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) corn and soybean futures which breached resistance at $3.00 a bushel in corn and $8.00 a bushel in soybeans, caught buyers by surprise, the traders said.
"Soybean and corn futures prices have jumped too fast, buyers are likely to stay sidelined this week," a trader said.
On the CBOT's Project A overnight trading system, March corn futures pushed up through $3.00 a bushel on Monday while May soybeans broke the $8.00 level.
Traders said the U.S. corn and soybean rallies would boost local buyers' interest in Argentine corn and Brazilian soybeans.
"The recent rise in U.S. futures prices makes the Argentine corn and Brazil soybeans more attractive alternatives to Taiwan buyers," a trader said.

Taiwan buyers would consider buying Argentine corn if the prices were about US$5 a tonne lower than U.S. corn, he said. The trader said Brazil soybeans would be considered if the prices were about US$10 a tonne lower than U.S. soybeans.
Local listed flour prices on Monday ranged between T$14.55 to T$15.68 per kg for Taipei delivery, unchanged from a week earlier.
U.S. Pacific Northwest to Taiwan freight rates were quoted at about US$14.50 a tonne and from the Gulf of Mexico between US$25.00 and US$25.50 a tonne, both for Panamax-sized March shipments.
